difference: Dense radii use a true ALL UNSPECIFIED RADII default only while all exceptions have callouts; matching fillets share the same presentation.
reason: The stream requests a general radius note. Python origin/main annotations/_edge_callouts.py::radius_jobs groups blend and fillet families separately into counted leaders. Rust combines equal displayed radius claims, preserves an established fillet leader for a mixed exception group, and removes same-value fillet leaders only after the default is drawable. An omitted or unsafe exception withdraws the default, restoring missing findings instead of assigning the wrong radius. CGB245 and CTC-01 regressions check this distinction. Bare pins preserve the consolidated owner and default; only original authored positioning choices override grouping, independently of the carrier filled into the effective Spec. The CGB245 bare-pin test checks exact label, geometry, claims, IDs and zero missing coverage, and failed with 18x R4 instead of 28x R4 before the correction.

difference: Same-face ownership replaces only the boss diameter; its independently required height survives.
reason: Python origin/main recognition_ownership.py::boss_blend_owner_pairs absorbs the entire boss only when an emitted envelope carries its length. Rust's shared lint::bosses::boss_owner proves a unique nonempty exact face match, matching principal axis and diameter within 0.15 mm of twice the blend radius. The radius replaces the duplicate diameter, while existing boss-height planning and consolidation retain or cover its length. tests/dims_blends.rs checks both full-span and shorter bosses, equal unrelated bosses and absent face evidence.

difference: Automatic blend notes carry Annotation.satisfies identities rather than Python registry handles; authored prose carries none.
reason: Exact satisfaction identities remain required, but are insufficient without an identifiable presentation. Full drawing lint accepts automatic ALL UNSPECIFIED RADII notes only with matching values and explicit callouts for other radii. Scoped and representative XYZ notes grant no authority. Authored prose has no satisfaction identities. Hide/move/unplaced, duplicate and removed-identity tests remain.

difference: Unsafe free blend leaders are withdrawn instead of replaced by representative XYZ notes. The default is withdrawn when any exception cannot be drawn.
reason: Python origin/main annotations/_edge_callouts.py::radius_jobs refuses missing physical surface selection. Python tests/test_issue_1187_unroutable_leaders.py documents Policy B: retain a required leader with a logged routing cost when no clear route exists. For automatic blend additions this stream instead requires no new radius clutter, so obstructed free blend leaders are withheld with blend_callout_dropped and exact missing coverage. Explicit author placement/tolerance choices remain literal, with their geometry findings. This is a deliberate conservative difference, not equivalence to Policy B; representative XYZ notes were an erroneous fallback and are removed.

difference: Removing a radius exception withdraws its dependent blanket default and restores any fillet leader that default conveyed; unrelated ink stays fixed.
reason: A true ALL UNSPECIFIED RADII default cannot survive an omitted exception of another value. Python origin/main annotations/_edge_callouts.py::radius_jobs has independent counted groups and no automatic default, so it has no such dependency. FTC-06 removing d:f:fillet:9/fillet.radius must withdraw the default and restore d:f:fillet:6/fillet.radius. tests/placement.rs and tests/trust_rules.rs check the exact restored label and geometry against hiding the note, requires an explicit note refusal caused by a radius exception, and retains every unrelated sheet/view/dimension placement assertion.
